picks.title: Taste cannot be delegated
picks.excerpt: An argument that as AI makes everyone a 'creator', taste and editorial judgment become the scarce design skill that can't be handed to a model — and that 'design by committee' dies precisely because someone still has to own the call. A design-leadership lens on where humans stay decisive in an AI workflow.
picks.rationale: Freshest, sharpest thesis in the pool — frames where designers stay decisive as AI commoditizes production, directly shaping how a design lead owns the call tomorrow.

picks.title: The interface has left the building
picks.excerpt: How chat, voice, and agentic AI are rewriting the first principles of UX — as the screen stops being the primary surface, designers have to rethink flows, affordances, and control for interfaces that are generated and negotiated at runtime rather than laid out in advance.
picks.rationale: High-novelty first-principles take on post-screen, agentic UX — distinct from the taste piece and useful for designers rethinking flows for runtime-generated interfaces.

picks.title: Design the Moment an AI Agent Needs Human Input
picks.excerpt: A recovery-first interaction model for long-running AI tasks: how to design the handoff points — interruptions, approvals, expiring decisions, safe resume — where an autonomous agent must pause for a human. Concrete UX patterns for agentic products.
picks.rationale: Most actionable card — concrete agentic-UX handoff patterns (interruptions, approvals, safe resume) a designer can apply directly, and it diversifies away from the two UX Collective essays.

picks.title: OpenAI is so back... GPT-5.6 Sol first look
picks.excerpt: Fireship's fast hands-on first look at OpenAI's newly released GPT-5.6 Sol model and what it means for AI-assisted building.
picks.rationale: Adds the social/creator-medium angle with a distinct URL — a hands-on take on GPT-5.6 Sol framed for builders, complementing the essay-heavy pool.
